title: Wise Words
subtitle: WITH MARCO REYES  ·  STORY NIGHT

segments.head: TONIGHT: THE DARK SIGN
segments.author: Wise Words
lines: Good evening, everyone.
I'm Marco Reyes, and this is Wise Words.
Tonight's story is about Roz Pelletier, an airplane riveter from Wichita, Kansas.
Every night she drove past the Starlite Diner and its neon sign, dark for twenty-five years.

segments.head: CHAPTER 1: SAME OLD ROAD
segments.quote: Live all you can; it's a mistake not to.
segments.author: Henry James
lines: On her forty-fourth birthday, Roz ate cake alone. Same job, same road, twenty years.
Her dad Gene called, sang badly, then read her a line from the novelist Henry James:
Live all you can; it's a mistake not to.
Next morning, she asked old Lupe at the diner if she could fix the sign. Lupe said, Light it, and you get free pie for life.

segments.head: CHAPTER 2: LEARNING NEON
segments.quote: Self-education is, I firmly believe, the only kind of education there is.
segments.author: Isaac Asimov
lines: Roz knew rivets. She did not know neon.
At the library, a book by the science writer Isaac Asimov had one line circled:
Self-education is, I firmly believe, the only kind of education there is.
So she taught herself, and found Walt, an eighty-one-year-old sign man who still bent glass in his garage.

segments.head: CHAPTER 3: BROKEN GLASS
segments.quote: We should regret our mistakes and learn from them, but never carry them forward into the future with us.
segments.author: L. M. Montgomery
lines: Neon tubes are glass, bent by hand over a flame. Roz broke twenty of them.
She called Walt and said, I'm no good at this. He read her Lucy Maud Montgomery, who wrote Anne of Green Gables:
We should regret our mistakes and learn from them, but never carry them forward into the future with us.
So she swept up, took notes, and tube twenty-two came out smooth.

segments.head: CHAPTER 4: DOING IT RIGHT
segments.quote: The secret of joy in work is contained in one word — excellence. To know how to do something well is to enjoy it.
segments.author: Pearl S. Buck
lines: A guy at the hardware store said, Just use cheap plastic lights. Nobody will know.
Then Walt mailed her a line from the novelist Pearl S. Buck:
The secret of joy in work is contained in one word, excellence. To know how to do something well is to enjoy it.
Roz would know. So every letter got real glass. Around the letter L, she started having fun.

segments.head: CHAPTER 5: THE LONG WAIT
segments.quote: Patience, n. A minor form of despair, disguised as a virtue.
segments.author: Ambrose Bierce
lines: Then the transformer that powers the sign was back-ordered. Six weeks.
Lupe slid her some pie and quoted Ambrose Bierce, the old newspaper wit:
Patience, noun. A minor form of despair, disguised as a virtue.
Roz snorted pie laughing. Then she quit fretting and painted the frame cherry red.

segments.head: CHAPTER 6: THE GLOW
segments.quote: The past is never dead. It's not even past.
segments.author: William Faulkner
lines: The night it lit up, half of Wichita parked on the street. Pink and blue, buzzing like summer.
Old couples held hands again. Gene cried and blamed the onions. Lupe quoted William Faulkner:
The past is never dead. It's not even past.
Then she handed Roz a fork. Roz is on slice number forty.

segments.head: THAT'S TONIGHT'S STORY
segments.quote: Live fully. Teach yourself. Drop old mistakes. Do it well. Laugh while you wait. Light up the past.
segments.author: Marco Reyes
lines: That's tonight's story.
Live fully. Teach yourself. Drop old mistakes. Do it well. Laugh while you wait. Light up the past.
I tried to fix my porch light once. The fire department still sends me a Christmas card.
I'm Marco Reyes. Good night.
